 Updated: 10:48 PM CST Nov 19, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Scott Reister Sports Director DES MOINES, Iowa — It's not every day a swimmer from North High School in Des Moines wins a state title in the water. In fact, it had been over a decade.
 On Friday, Haylie Weinheimer changed that with a championship performance. The UNI-bound senior won the 100-yard backstroke at the IGHSAU State Swimming and Diving Championships. Weinheimer is the first champion from Des Moines Public Schools since 2012.
 Advertisement On Thursday, coach Scott Weinheimer, Haylie's uncle, honored Haylie and her teammates with a community celebration at the high school pool.
 "I don't even remember that much of the race itself," Haylie said. "I just remember swimming it and touching the wall and being like, 'Oh my gosh.' I knew I could do it, and I expected it to happen, but I also didn't at the same time. It was really it was awesome. It was great hearing my name. But then, Scott, my uncle, my coach being able to give me the medal and do that moment together. This has been a goal of mine but also been a goal of his. It was even more special to be able to take in that moment with him." 
 "That was pretty cool," Scott Weinheimer said. "Getting to walk out there and put that medal around her neck. She earned it."
